about: #486 read-aloud-pieces: the pieces a block's text is read in. src/render.rs read_pieces and the page's readPieces (web/src/core/speech/) are both held to every case here. A case with "alone": true is the whole of a message that is one block (read-chunk-balance).

cases.name: typed bullets
pieces: Settings sync is live on both servers (build bac092ae), #457 settings-server-side:

• Every setting outside "Screen and keys" is now stored on the server and shared by all your devices: read mode, collapsed lines, pack/unpack and card states, sort order, read-aloud prefs, and so on. A change on one device reaches your other open devices live, without a reload.
• "Screen and keys" (text size, width, bar placement, Enter-sends, single-key shortcuts) stays per-device, and its heading now says "(client side)" in small, faint text.

• First load on each device seeds the server with that device's values only where the server has none, so nothing newer is overwritten. Load your phone and your desktop once each and they'll converge.

Known limits: a setting holding several entries (e.g. per-thread card states) merges as a whole, so two devices editing different entries at the same moment can lose one side's edit. Migration against your real devices hasn't been exercised outside tests, so tell me if anything looks reset.

cases.name: long paragraph
pieces: The cache follows the same rules as the store does. Newer content replaces older content whenever a read brings it, and a deletion leaves a contentless tombstone behind it.

A pushed event can never resurrect a deleted message, and only a read that started after the deletion can bring it back. That keeps the two copies honest with each other. Slack's forward feed is additions-only: what is new since a point never reports edits or deletes.

An edit or delete of an older message is therefore noticed only when someone loads that range again, which can be hours later on a quiet channel. The cheap improvement is to subscribe the hint to updates and deletions too, and re-read just the affected message.
